solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Enemy captured sailors' pad, shattering false hopes and expectations

indicators.note: the enemy word holds the rearranged letters inside it, as a captor holds a prisoner

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

indicators.note: the sailors' pad letters are broken up and put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A foe raids a sailors' lodging and destroys their comfortable illusions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' looks like the place being shattered, but it is fodder; 'shattering' gives OOLSPARADIS, the anagram of the fodder, which 'captured' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a state of happiness built on illusion, which is a set of false hopes and expectations.

clue.text: Jeweller who was known as a good egg?

definitions.text: Jeweller who was known as a good egg?

parts.words: Jeweller who was known as a good egg?
parts.note: a 'good egg' is a decent person, but here it hints at the Russian jeweller famous for his jewelled Easter eggs

explanation.surface: A craftsman remembered as a thoroughly decent fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Carl Fabergé made the famous jewelled Easter eggs for the Russian tsars, so he was literally known for good eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian goldsmith whose house produced ornate jewelled eggs is the most famous jeweller linked with eggs.

clue.text: Tender embrace for Scotsman returning for a spell in the background

indicators.note: the offer word wraps its arms round the reversed Scotsman

parts.note: to tender is to offer

indicators.note: returning means the word for a Scotsman is read backwards

parts.note: Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman, from the common surname prefix

explanation.surface: A tender hug for a returning Scot, briefly out of the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives CAM; 'Tender' is a verb here, not an adjective describing the embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done out of shot of the filming lens is not seen, so it happens out of view, in the background.

clue.text: Fixes and marks locations

definitions.meaning: identifies or pins down, as in fixing a position

explanation.surface: Someone pinpoints and labels places on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: to identify or pinpoint, small blemishes, and particular places.

clue.text: Make notes on ornamentation, discounting minor repair

indicators.note: the letters of the word minor are taken out of the longer word's pool
what is left is mended into a new order, like repairing something broken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A restorer records the decoration while ignoring a small fix.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters M, I, N, O, R ('discounting minor') from ORNAMENTATION and rearrange ('repair') what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To add commentary or explanatory remarks to a text is to make notes on it.

clue.text: Fight fish clinging to hook without starting to grimace

indicators.note: the fish word holds on to the end of the shortened hook word
the hook loses a letter, so the word appears without it

parts.note: a gaff is a hook used to land large fish

indicators.note: starting to means take the first letter of grimace

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: An angler grimly fights a fish caught on the hook.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFF loses G (the start of 'grimace') to give AFF; RAY clings on behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl or public fight is called an affray, especially in legal language.

clue.text: Knowing ring has it but circle doesn't!

parts.words: ring has it but circle doesn't!
parts.note: a ring of string or wire encloses something within its loop, while a drawn circle is just an outline; playful hint at being included

explanation.surface: A riddle contrasting a ring and a circle, as if one were in on a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being informed and included in what is going on, hence knowing.

clue.text: Deception over stealing graduate correspondence

indicators.note: the reversed lie takes the graduate in, as a thief takes goods
in a down clue over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a lie is a deception
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A fraud involving a stolen degree certificate turns up in the letters.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' gives EIL, an upward reading; 'stealing' means taking in.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic messages are a form of written correspondence.

clue.text: Central courts cover confident cupidinous capitalist!

indicators.note: the central pair sits on either side of the confident word, covering it
central means take the middle letters of courts

parts.note: sure means confident

explanation.surface: An alliterative jab at a greedy financier sure of himself in the law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging excessive interest is a greedy capitalist; cupidinous means covetous.

clue.text: Clown is expert in no time, which isn't special

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert

indicators.note: the word for in no time is shown without the special letter

parts.note: soon means in no time

explanation.surface: A clown who is an expert in a jiffy, though not out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon is a fool or joker, a synonym for a clown.

clue.text: Bigwigs have Reg thrown out of stagecraft school

indicators.note: the letters of Reg are expelled from the longer word's pool
what remains is trained into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bigwigs get a student named Reg expelled from drama school.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R, E, G ('Reg thrown out of') from STAGECRAFT and rearrange ('school') the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy, important people are fat cats, an informal term for bigwigs.

clue.text: Loads of paper

parts.note: a ream is a fixed bundle of paper sheets

explanation.surface: A plain description of a great quantity of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is 500 sheets, and colloquially reams means great quantities, especially of writing.

clue.text: One's going places with time for composer, vigilant at heart

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer

indicators.note: at heart means only the middle of the vigilant word is kept, its outer letters dropped

parts.note: alert means vigilant

explanation.surface: Someone making progress, with time for music and watchful inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the heart of ALERT is used, giving LER.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller is literally someone who goes from place to place.

clue.text: A long time heading off philanthropist gripping broken rein

indicators.note: the shortened name holds the rearranged letters inside it
heading off means the first letter of the philanthropist's name is removed

parts.note: J. Paul Getty was an oil magnate and philanthropist

indicators.note: broken means the letters of rein are rearranged

explanation.surface: A long wait while a benefactor grips a snapped rein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves ETTY; 'broken' gives ERNI. The philanthropist is the American oil billionaire J. Paul Getty.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, and colloquially any very long time.

clue.text: Not one idiot in US city is a lightweight

parts.note: none means not one

indicators.note: the idiot word goes inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is short for New York
tit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about a fool in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: TIT is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody of no importance or influence is a lightweight.

clue.text: Runner eating lunch at first is seen to be on course

indicators.note: the runner word takes the letter inside, as if eating it

parts.note: a gofer is an errand runner

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter of lunch

explanation.surface: A runner grabbing lunch looks to be on track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on course' means on a golf course, not on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone playing a round is found on a golf course.

clue.text: The cheek of it — Pip can fly off

indicators.note: off means the letters of Pip can fly go astray and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An indignant reaction to someone named Pip flying away.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippancy is disrespectful lack of seriousness, a kind of cheek or impudence.

clue.text: Generate fresh drink

indicators.note: fresh means the letters of generate are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: An instruction to brew a new drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfermented tea popular in East Asia is a drink.

clue.text: Fuzzy George is wet …

parts.note: rainy means wet

explanation.surface: George looks fuzzy because he is soaked; it runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A grainy image is indistinct or blurred, that is fuzzy.

clue.text: Questions the king's misfortunes

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is the abbreviation for King George
ills are misfortunes

explanation.surface: A query about a monarch's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to question them intensely; both are verbs.

clue.text: … but the fat Duke is fantastic!

parts.note: ripping is old British slang for excellent or fantastic

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: George is soaked, but the plump duke is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripping is dated British slang for marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: The fat that runs from roasting meat is used for cooking in Britain.

clue.text: "Dress will detract from the man" says Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner's slips swap the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: to mar is to detract from or spoil
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A warning that clothing spoils its wearer, attributed to Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: MAR GENT with the first letters swapped becomes GAR MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress is an item of clothing, an example of the wider category.

clue.text: Extent to which outside line is no good to horses at the start

indicators.note: outside means take the outer letters of line
at the start means take the first letters of to and horses

explanation.surface: Racing talk about how far a horse on the outside line is behind at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Length is measurement end to end, and so extent; it is also a racing margin.

clue.text: Certain since recording that some of it is fake

indicators.note: some of means only part of the run of words is taken, the answer lying inside it

explanation.surface: A claim that part of a recording is not genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insincere is pretending feelings they lack, hence fake.

clue.text: Costly pickle

definitions.meaning: to soak in liquid, as when pickling

explanation.surface: A jar of expensive preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an exorbitant price, and to soak food in a liquid such as brine.

clue.text: Introducing this animal, primarily inhabiting Central America

definitions.text: Introducing this animal, primarily inhabiting Central America

indicators.note: introducing means take the opening letters of the following words
central means take the middle letter of America

explanation.surface: A presenter introduces a creature native to Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapir is a hoofed mammal with a short trunk, found mainly in Central and South America.

clue.text: Indian police HQ in Elizabethan armoury

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the run of letters of the next words

explanation.surface: An Indian police station housed in an old Tudor weapons store.
explanation.definitionFit: Thana is the Hindi word used in India for a police station.

clue.text: Eyeing up Heather, who's always in

indicators.note: the always word goes inside the heather word

parts.note: ling is a common heather
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Someone ogling a woman named Heather who never goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a name; it is the plant ling.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone suggestively, eyeing them up.

clue.text: Novice grounded, getting an E in the end (not D)

indicators.text: getting an E in the end (not D)
indicators.note: the closing letter of the grounded word is swapped, an E taking the place of D

parts.note: trained means well grounded in a skill

explanation.surface: A beginner is let down, getting an E grade rather than a D.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as exam grades.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is someone still learning, a trainee.

clue.text: Will one's services be needed after watching horror movie?

definitions.text: Will one's services be needed after watching horror movie?

parts.words: Will one's services be needed after watching horror movie?
parts.note: the horror movie hints at Hitchcock's Psycho, and a therapist might be needed after a fright

explanation.surface: A wry question about therapy after a scary film.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitchcock's horror film Psycho is the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist who treats mental distress might be called after a terrifying experience.
